discoveries: (1) Inside this sandbox `TMPDIR=/tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-123` is read-only, so Python's `tempfile` falls back to the working directory and pytest writes `pytest-of-usain/` into the worktree. (2) The sandbox runs in its own PID namespace (the shell is pid 1). `safe_restart` reads `/proc` and `/proc/net/tcp`, so it only sees processes and listeners in the caller's namespace; the dispatcher (W2-121) must call it outside such a sandbox. (3) For a planted script, `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` reads `<interpreter> <script> serve`, so the "is this our serve" check compares the last two arguments (resolved against the process's cwd) rather than requiring exactly two.
risks: (1) `preexec_fn` is documented as unsafe in a threaded parent; CPython handles it in practice and a failure fails closed (no start). (2) `safe_restart` on a hung server probes twice (the re-check before the stop), so at the defaults it can take about 240 s before it acts. (3) `pytest-of-usain/` (28K, 9 inodes, only pytest's own temp dirs) is left untracked in the worktree: `rm -rf` was refused. (4) `settings.cpus` reports the configured list intersected with the caller's allowed CPUs (what is actually applied), in canonical form, so `"8,2-5"` reads back as `"2-5,8"`.
